title: `join_where`: a streaming range join with the rows of a cross join and a filter
verdict: the pairs a cross join and a filter keep; one or two inequalities run as a streaming range join, an equality with an inequality as a hash join with a fused predicate
description: `left.join_where(right, *predicates)` keeps the pairs of rows for which every predicate is true: the rows of `left.join(right, how="cross")` filtered by the predicates. A NULL operand never matches (its comparison is NULL, not true). On doubles Polars compares as everywhere else: NaN is above every number and equal to itself (polars-nan-order, polars-nan-equality), and the probes compare canonical keys, so `-0.0` and `0.0` do not arise.

Physical plan under the streaming engine (`show_graph(engine="streaming", plan_stage="physical")`): one inequality, and two inequalities, run as a `range-join` node, which streams; an equality with an inequality runs as an `equi-join` with the inequality as a fused predicate; `join(how="cross")` is a `cross-join` node. None is an in-memory fallback (polars-exec-streaming-fallback).

sverify's Polars translation uses it for a join without an equality key whose condition has a range comparison of a left-only expression with a right-only one that can raise nothing (`Translator.range_join`, #1447, rulings 162 and 164). The whole condition, with its guard, then filters the matches as before.
reference: `Rel.join` keeps the pairs whose condition is TRUE (`isTrue_and3`). The range join gives the same pairs; the rest of the condition is evaluated on them as on the cross join's, and a pair one conjunct makes not TRUE is in no allowed result (D16), so the run may return where the reference may raise on such a pair (ruling 164).

evidence.note: Hypothesis, the translation's range join against its cross join and filter on the same inputs: NULL, NaN, both zeros, infinities, duplicates, empty sides; inner, left, semi and anti joins; one and two inequalities, a mirrored one, one beside another conjunct.
the physical plan of the translated frame has a range-join node and no cross-join

provenance.notes: Probed by hand first on two small frames: `join_where(a > b)`, `(a > b, a <= c + 3)` and `(k == kr, a >= b)` collected on the streaming engine equal the cross join filtered by the same predicates, with NULL and NaN in a, b and the keys; `show_graph` gave range-join, range-join and equi-join.
